newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK govt backs property developers' self-regulation.
newsitem.headline: HK govt backs property developers' self-regulation.

text.p: The Hong Kong government on Wednesday welcomed self-regulatory measures proposed by property developers to curb speculation.

"We welcome the introduction of new sales arrangements announced by the Real Estate Developers Association of Hong Kong (REDA)...as a first step to dampen speculation through companies," Secretary of Housing Dominic Wong said.

Wong said the government had urged the REDA to adopt additional steps to help end the recent bout of speculative activity, and that the association's members would adopt the following measures with immediate effect:
* To ban resale of uncompleted flats bought by companies by changing company directorships in the time between registration for purchase and the signing of sales and purchase agreements;
* To limit flat sales to companies to the last 15 percent of each batch of flats, leaving the rest to genuine end-users;
* To promulgate clearly in sales brochures and newspaper advertisements the total number of flats available for pre-sale in each housing development;
* To ensure that the 10 percent of flats allowed for internal sales to persons connected to the developer only goes to genuine end-users;
The measures apply to flats sold under the Consent Scheme, meaning flats built on land released by the government, but REDA will also encourage members to adopt the measures on all flats.
The key measures target purchase of flats by companies.
Speculators can register to buy flats as a shell company, then sell the company and change the directorship to get around a ban on the resale of uncompleted flats before occupation.
Wong said the ban on resale by way of changing company directorships would effectively tackle speculation by ensuring parity between company and individual purchasers.
The requirement to provide clearer information ensured a more transparent market, while the restriction on internal sales closed a loophole for potential abuse, he added.
"Taken together, they will help to protect the interests of genuine flat buyers and greatly dampen speculation in the residential property market," he said.
Wong stressed the government would continue to monitor the market and the effectiveness of the new measures.

"If voluntary compliance with these measures by developers does not achieve the desired objectives, we will not hesitate to take action to introduce appropriate measures to restore the proper operation of the market," he said.
